title: CORNER Client Onboarding Guide
summary: Step-by-step guide for taking a signed Corner client from contract to live operations. The 14-day journey. Who does what, when, and how. Built for Patrik and the AOM ops team.
content:
CORNER Client Onboarding Guide

Author: Steve (AI Advisory Lead) Date: 2026-03-16 For: Patrik (client relationship), Ash (operations), the AOM system (agent configuration) Scope: The 14-day journey from signed contract to autonomous Corner operations

The Onboarding Promise

"In two weeks, your AI team will be running your back office."

That's the promise. Every step below serves it. If any step takes longer than expected, the rest compress. The client has a working Corner instance by Day 14. No exceptions.

Pre-Onboarding (Before Day 1)

Trigger: Client signs contract and first payment clears.

Patrik does:

  • Send welcome message (personal, not templated): "You're in. We start Monday. I'll send you a link to get started."
  • Schedule kickoff call (30 minutes, within 48 hours of signing)
  • Add client to AOM internal tracking (Paige's client health system)

System does:

  • Create client folder in AOM-EA: projects/clients/[client-name]/
  • Initialize client files: AGENT.md, context.md, onboarding-log.md
  • Add to admin panel (when C4 ships)

Day 1-2: Discovery

Goal: Understand the business deeply enough to configure their Corner instance.

Kickoff Call (30 minutes)

Agenda:

  1. Quick introductions (2 min)
  2. "Walk me through your business" (10 min)
    • What do you do? Who are your clients?
    • How many people on your team?
    • What tools do you currently use? (QuickBooks, spreadsheets, calendar, email, project management)
  3. "What breaks?" (10 min)
    • What falls through the cracks?
    • Where do you spend the most time on admin?
    • What's the thing you wish someone else handled?
  4. "What does a perfect day look like?" (5 min)
    • If everything ran smoothly, what would change about your day?
    • What would you do with an extra 10 hours a week?
  5. Next steps (3 min)
    • "I'm going to build your AI team based on everything you just told me. You'll have a link to your office within a week."
    • "If you can share access to your calendar and email (read-only), the agents start learning your patterns immediately."

Output: Patrik writes projects/clients/[client-name]/context.md with:

  • Business description (2-3 sentences)
  • Team members (names, roles)
  • Current tools
  • Top 3 pain points
  • Communication style preference (brief vs. detailed, formal vs. casual)
  • Industry-specific context (for a contractor: trades, typical project size, service area; for a CPA: firm size, specialties, software, busy season)

Access Setup (Day 1-2)

Request from client (via email, keep it simple):

  • Google Calendar: read-only access (AOM connects via API)
  • Email: forwarding address for automated triage (or OAuth connection)
  • CRM/contacts: export of client list (CSV or spreadsheet)
  • Any other tools they want integrated (QuickBooks, etc.)

AOM sets up:

  • Calendar agent connected
  • Email triage agent connected (read-only initially, no sending)
  • Client list imported into context

Day 3-5: Configuration

Goal: Build the client's Corner instance with their data and their agents.

Agent Selection

Based on the discovery call, select from the agent roster:

Agent Type When to Include Example Trigger from Discovery
Operations Always Every client gets this. The chief of staff.
Calendar Always Every client gets this.
Email Triage If they get 20+ emails/day "I spend an hour every morning on email"
Outreach If they need new clients/leads "We need more business"
Client Comms If they have ongoing client relationships "Following up with clients is our biggest gap"
Finance/Invoicing If they handle their own invoicing "We're always chasing payments"
Content/Social If they want social media presence "We should be posting but never do"
Scheduling/Dispatch Construction: crew scheduling "Coordinating the crew schedule is a nightmare"
Estimating Construction: bid preparation "Estimates take forever"
Document Collection CPA: client document tracking "Chasing clients for documents is our biggest pain"
Deadline Tracking CPA/Law: regulatory deadlines "We can't afford to miss a deadline"

Starter tier: 3 agents (Operations, Calendar, Email Triage) Growth tier: 6 agents (add Outreach, Client Comms, and one industry-specific) Scale tier: 10 agents (full roster)

Agent Configuration

For each selected agent, write:

  • System prompt (personality, communication style, role description)
  • Initial context (pulled from client's context.md)
  • First tasks (2-3 tasks per agent to have them working before the client sees the office)
  • Skills to install (from the skills library)

Room Setup

  • Select industry theme (Construction HQ, CPA Office, General Business)
  • Place agents in rooms per the floor plan
  • Configure room names (customize to client's business)
  • Set default HUD layout (Checklist mode for new users, they can switch later)

Pre-Seeding

Before the client sees their office, agents should already have work done:

  • Calendar agent: scanned upcoming week, organized by priority
  • Email agent: categorized last 50 emails (if access granted)
  • Operations agent: created initial priority list from discovery call notes
  • Outreach agent: drafted 3 follow-up emails for stale leads (if client provided contact list)

This is the "wow" moment. The client opens their office and their agents have already done work. Not an empty dashboard. A working team.

Day 5-7: Soft Launch

Goal: Client opens their Corner office for the first time. Guided experience.

The Reveal

Patrik sends the link with a personal message: "Your office is ready. Your team's been working since yesterday. Here's what they've done so far."

Include a screenshot of the isometric view showing agents in rooms. Make it visual.

First Session (Guided, 20 minutes)

Patrik walks the client through their office (screen share or in-person):

  1. Tour the office (5 min)

    • Show each agent's room
    • Click one agent, show the chat interface
    • "This is Operations. She's already organized your priorities for the week."

  2. Chat with an agent (5 min)

    • Let the client type a question: "What do I have today?"
    • Calendar agent responds with their actual schedule
    • Let them ask a follow-up: "Move my 2pm to 3pm"
    • Calendar agent confirms

  3. Show Checklist mode (3 min)

    • "Here's the simple view. Every task, every agent, one list."
    • Show how to add a task
    • Show how to assign to an agent

  4. Show Megaboard (3 min)

    • "Here's your stats view. This fills up over time as agents do more work."
    • Show hours saved, tasks completed (will be small since it's day 1)

  5. Set expectations (4 min)

    • "This week, just use it. Talk to your agents. Give them tasks. Ask them questions. The more you use it, the better they get."
    • "If anything feels wrong, message me directly. I'll fix it same day."
    • "Next week we do a check-in to see what's working and what needs adjustment."

Success Criteria for Soft Launch

The client:

  • Logged in at least once
  • Sent at least one message to an agent
  • Saw agents with real work (not empty)
  • Understands the three modes (even if they only use one)
  • Knows how to reach Patrik if something breaks

Day 7-10: Active Usage

Goal: Client uses Corner daily. Agents handle increasing amounts of real work.

Daily Monitoring (AOM Internal)

Operations agent in AOM's system monitors the client's activity:

  • Is the client logging in? (Target: daily by day 7)
  • Are they chatting with agents? (Target: 3+ messages/day)
  • Are agents completing tasks? (Target: 5+ tasks/week)
  • Any errors or agent failures?

If the client isn't logging in by Day 7, Patrik sends a gentle nudge: "Hey [Name], your agents have been working on [specific thing]. Check it out when you get a chance."

Adjustment Window

Based on observed usage, Patrik makes adjustments:

  • Client only uses Calendar? Make Calendar agent more proactive (morning briefings, conflict detection)
  • Client ignores Email Triage? Maybe they prefer handling email themselves. Reduce email agent's scope.
  • Client asks Operations for things Finance agent should handle? Route the request, tune the agents.

This is the fine-tuning phase. The initial configuration is never perfect. The adjustments make it personal.

Day 10-12: Check-In

Goal: Confirm value. Catch friction. Lock in the relationship.

Check-In Call (15 minutes)

Agenda:

  1. "How's it going?" (3 min)

    • Open-ended. Let them talk.
    • Listen for: what they love, what frustrates them, what they haven't tried

  2. "Let me show you what your agents have done" (5 min)

    • Share the Megaboard: hours saved, tasks completed
    • Highlight specific wins: "Your Calendar agent handled 12 scheduling changes this week"
    • If ROI is visible: "Based on these first two weeks, you're saving about X hours a month"

  3. "What should we add?" (4 min)

    • Ask if there are tasks they do manually that they'd want an agent to handle
    • If Growth/Scale tier: suggest adding another agent based on observed patterns
    • If Starter tier: show what's available on upgrade (but don't push)

  4. "Anything broken?" (3 min)

    • Direct ask. Let them flag issues without feeling awkward.
    • Commit to fixing anything within 24 hours.

Post-Check-In Actions

  • Fix any reported issues (same day)
  • Add any new agents or skills requested
  • Update client's context.md with learnings from check-in
  • Update Paige's client health with engagement metrics

Day 12-14: Autonomous Operations

Goal: The client's Corner runs without daily AOM involvement. Agents handle operations independently.

Transition to Autonomous

By Day 12, the agents should be:

  • Handling daily calendar management without client prompting
  • Triaging email (if connected) and surfacing priorities
  • Maintaining a task list that reflects reality
  • Following up on items the client assigned
  • Producing weekly recaps (when C5 ships)

The signal it's working: The client stops thinking about Corner as a new tool and starts treating the agents like team members. They say "my Operations agent" not "that AI thing."

Ongoing Support Model

After Day 14:

  • Monthly check-in: 15-minute call. Review Megaboard stats, discuss adjustments, answer questions.
  • Async support: Client can message Patrik any time. Response within 4 hours business hours.
  • Quarterly review: Deep dive into ROI, feature roadmap preview, potential tier upgrade discussion.
  • Agent updates: AOM pushes skill updates and agent improvements via OTA (when C4 ships). Client gets better without doing anything.

Onboarding Timeline Summary

Day Phase Key Activity Who
0 Pre-onboarding Welcome message, schedule kickoff Patrik
1-2 Discovery Kickoff call, access setup Patrik + Client
3-5 Configuration Agent selection, room setup, pre-seeding AOM system + Patrik
5-7 Soft Launch Client opens office, guided first session Patrik + Client
7-10 Active Usage Daily use, monitoring, adjustments Client + AOM monitoring
10-12 Check-In Review call, fix issues, optimize Patrik + Client
12-14 Autonomous System runs independently System (AOM monitors)
14+ Ongoing Monthly calls, async support, updates Patrik (monthly)

Common Failure Modes (and How to Prevent Them)

1. Client doesn't log in after Day 1. Prevention: Pre-seed agents with real work. The client opens the office and sees value immediately. Nudge on Day 3 if no login.

2. Client asks agents questions they can't answer. Prevention: Write thorough context files during configuration. The more context the agents have, the better they answer. If an agent gives a bad answer, fix the context file within hours.

3. Client expects human-level conversation. Prevention: Set expectations during the guided session. "They're incredibly capable at tasks. They're not perfect at freeform conversation. Give them specific instructions and they'll outperform."

4. Client doesn't know what to ask. Prevention: Operations agent proactively sends a morning briefing: "Good morning. Here's what's on your plate today: [3 priorities]. Want me to handle any of these?" The agent initiates, not the client.

5. Client's team doesn't adopt. Prevention: This is a C7 problem (multi-user). For now, Corner is the owner's tool. The owner delegates to Corner, not the team. Position it as: "Your assistant, not a team tool."

6. Client wants to cancel during the first month. Prevention: The Day 10 check-in catches issues before they become cancellations. If a client wants to cancel, Patrik has a conversation (not Operations, not an email): "What's not working? Let me fix it this week." Most cancellation reasons are fixable.

Templates

Welcome Message Template

"[Name], welcome to Corner. You're in.

Your AI team starts building this week. I'm going to learn your business and configure everything for you. All you need to do is show up for a 30-minute kickoff call.

How does [day/time] work?

Patrik"

Check-In Message Template

"[Name], quick check-in on your Corner team.

Your agents have [specific metric: completed X tasks, handled Y calendar changes, triaged Z emails] in the last [timeframe].

Got 15 minutes this week to walk through what's working and tweak anything that isn't?

Patrik"

Nudge Message (If Client Isn't Logging In)

"[Name], your agents have been busy.

[Operations agent] organized your priorities for the week. [Calendar agent] flagged a scheduling conflict on Thursday. Might be worth a quick look.

[Link to their office]

Patrik"

The best onboarding is invisible. The client shouldn't feel like they're "setting up a tool." They should feel like they hired a team that showed up on Monday, already knew the business, and started working. That's the experience. Everything on this page serves it.
